skin_texture.roughness_basis: Reconstructed engineering value, not measured from a period person or calibrated capture.
skin_texture.identity_basis: Cleared reusable generic skin atlas; not a likeness, attested complexion, or source identifying any named/reconstructed resident.
skin_texture.uv_status: Source atlas and UV registration viewed in source diagnostics; final Blender export/LOD render validation remains outstanding.
skin_texture.female_appearance_status: The same author's female bronze atlas (skins01, CC0), replacing the male one whose beard shadow read as a man's jaw at 3 m (T-3434); photographic qualification remains open.

hair_component.appearance_basis: Cleared CC0 bun hair (RehmanPolanski, from the MakeHuman ponytail01), the hair drawn back smooth from the face to a bun at the back of the head, as the 1903 Wasson stereographs show a working woman's hair drawn up; its red velvet tie recoloured dark (T-3434). No personal appearance or photographic qualification is asserted.

eye_components.source_basis: Actual helper centers/axes; original opaque sclera/iris/pupil, reconstructed dimensions and brown color, not resident facts

label: Reconstructed 1904 cook's working dress (a dark print cotton dress with a plain bodice, long sleeves pushed up and rolled on the forearm and a full gathered skirt to the floor, a broad checked apron wrapping round the skirt with a square bib pinned on, a waistband and ties knotted behind, a dark cloth bound over the drawn-up hair, black shoes) on the shared portable female rig
basis: The T-3423 dress components (bodice and blouse fullness, gathered skirt, bib) re-cut and re-coloured as an older cook's print work dress, the sleeves cut back to the forearm and rolled, a broad checked apron wrapped round the skirt with its bib pinned on and no straps, a waistband and its ties knotted behind, a cloth bound over the hair and closed shoes, cut after the cooks the reference photographs show. Every amount and colour is reconstructed (tools/human_cook_1904.py, T-3479).
source_scope: C. L. Wasson's 1903 stereograph of an older cook at the kitchen table (LOC, no known restrictions) gives the dark long-sleeved blouse, the checked bib apron, the dark spotted skirt to the floor and the cloth bound over the hair; Underwood & Underwood's 1901 'Bridget' (LOC) an older Irish cook's long figured print dress with full sleeves and a broad checked apron wrapping round the skirt; Wasson's 1903 young woman at the same table (LOC) the sleeves pushed up the forearm at work. All are staged comic scenes, the 1901 one a caricature, none of Chicago or of Kate Ryan, and all are monochrome: the print and the check are drawn as their mean colour.

body_parameters.height_basis: The shared female engineering body; the variation kit draws height and build at runtime. Not a recorded height.
body_parameters.age_basis: Engineering body at the female kit base age 25. human-variation.js ages a person drawn in the town from their own record (hm08_variation_persons.json): born April 1850 by the 1900 census, 54 in 1904.
body_parameters.shape_basis: Equal cleared upstream female-young software-category blend, not inferred ancestry or a portrait

proof_variants.body_basis: CC0 adult-female graphical body and the generic cleared female skin are reconstructed authoring choices. Kate Ryan is an inferred person of the 1904 house (its cook in the 1900 census, born in Ireland; no source read says she was still there in July 1904); no picture of her is known, and no complexion, height or outfit of hers is asserted.

cook_components.evidence_choice: The brief asked for an Irish cook of fifty-four in her working dress, her own cut, not a recolour. The two older cooks of the reference pictures agree on a long print dress, a broad checked apron and the hair kept up and covered or drawn back; the 1903 cook's dark dress and bound head cloth are chosen over the 1901 caricature's light print, because hers is a photograph of a working cook nearer the scene date, and the 1901 apron's breadth round the skirt is kept. The sleeves are pushed up because she is at work at her kitchen door.

provenance.source_scope: A plain long-sleeved bodice with a narrow band at the neck, a little full in front, as both older cooks wear one; the dark colour follows the 1903 cook's dark blouse, the print is drawn as its mean colour, and the fullness and ease are reconstructed.
Sleeves pushed up the forearm at work, as the 1903 young woman at the kitchen table wears hers; how far up and the rolled band are reconstructed.
A full dark skirt to the floor, of the same print as the bodice, as both cooks wear it; the gathers, fullness and hem height are reconstructed.

A broad checked apron from the waist nearly to the hem, wrapping round the skirt past the hips, as the 1901 cook wears hers, with a square bib pinned on the bodice front as the 1903 cook's checked bib apron has; the check is drawn as its mean blue-grey, and its width and the bib's size are reconstructed.
The apron's band round the waist shows in the 1901 picture; its ties knotted at the back are not seen in either picture and are reconstructed.

A cloth bound over the drawn-up hair, as the 1903 cook wears one; its colour (a faded madder red, chosen to read as cloth over the hair, the picture showing only a dark cloth), its knot and its fit are reconstructed.
Black low shoes show under the 1901 cook's hem; their cut is reconstructed.
